source.version: Publisher journal article, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1910545, published 14 September 2026; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1910545 (PDF p. 1).

studies.label: Three-arm workflow experiment: argumentative essay followed by an unaided parallel essay

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Table 2 (columns Autonomous, Dependent, No-AI)
counts_source.quote: three-arm experiment (900 randomized; 659 in the primary analysis); Randomized 278 294 328; Primary analysis sample 222 225 212

arms.name: Autonomous
arms.description: Self-generation-first workflow: submit a position and outline before the AI panel opens, compare and judge disagreements with AI, and rewrite the final argument in the participant’s own words (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4–2.5).

arms.name: Dependent
arms.description: Direct-adoption workflow: ask AI to generate arguments and paragraphs and adopt its output with minimal changes; no required outline step (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4–2.5).

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Write independently without AI, search engines, or external materials (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5).

studies.task: Write a public-policy argumentative essay under the assigned workflow and then a parallel policy essay unaided, with the city-center car-ban and shorter-work-week topics counterbalanced across phases (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3).

ai_tool.name: Qwen3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen; Alibaba Cloud), official API embedded in the study platform
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.5; the model name is printed, but its release year and exact pinned version are not.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1.1: "The study was not formally preregistered"; a dated internal analysis plan preceded analysis.

estimates.outcome: Change in unaided reasoning quality from baseline to Phase 2
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Blind ratings of thesis clarity, evidence relevance and sufficiency, reasoning coherence, and counterarguments on a 1–7 rubric; rater means are the essay scores (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6). The recorded arm levels are the printed baseline-to-Phase-2 changes, not final-score levels (PDF p. 12, Section 4.5).

sources.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 4.5, first limitation: baseline-to-Phase-2 change scores
sources.quote: the no-AI arm was essentially unchanged (−0.02 on the 1–7 scale), the autonomous arm gained slightly (+0.17), and the dependent arm lost substantially (−0.49;

estimates.notes: Arm-level change means only. The paragraph does not label these means as covariate-adjusted and reports only an omnibus comparison across all arms. No pairwise difference, test, uncertainty, or standardized effect is printed for this change-score contrast; none is calculated or borrowed from the time-adjusted ANCOVA. Analysis-specific participant counts are not stated here, so they remain null rather than being inferred from degrees of freedom or assumed from the study’s primary-sample counts. Repeated baseline and transfer measurements do not make this a randomized within-person-order design. Both essays contributing to the change were unaided; the intervening workflow was randomized. The usefulness classification follows the reconciled screening form: this is the quality of reasoning in a policy argument, rather than a language-proficiency composite. A higher change means a greater improvement in this rated output quality.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Phase-2 reasoning-quality ANCOVAs, all three arm contrasts and all reported model, sample, attrition, imputation, and threshold sensitivity variants
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under extraction-spec Rule 5 because the estimated effect conditions on time measured after assignment. PDF p. 6, Section 2.8: "For Phase-2 (transfer) models, the covariates were baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task, and for Phase-1 models, baseline ability and Phase-1 time." PDF p. 4, Table 1 note explicitly says "the two time-on-task rows are post-treatment". Results are in PDF pp. 7–9, Sections 3.4–3.7, Figure 2, and PDF p. 10, Table 4. The Table 4 note states: "All models are ANCOVAs adjusting for baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task unless the speciﬁcation states otherwise; p-values are two-sided and uncorrected." Consequently the primary, robust-SE, single-rater, per-protocol, expanded-sample and imputation specifications are not exempt from the exclusion. Models additionally adjusting effort, earlier performance, or earlier duration also condition on post-treatment variables. The separately printed baseline-to-transfer change means in Section 4.5 are retained in estimates.

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Phase-2 idea diversity, Dependent versus No-AI, Autonomous versus No-AI, and Autonomous versus Dependent; additional Phase-1-duration adjustment
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under extraction-spec Rule 5 because the estimated effect conditions on time measured after assignment. PDF p. 6, Section 2.8: "For Phase-2 (transfer) models, the covariates were baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task, and for Phase-1 models, baseline ability and Phase-1 time." PDF p. 4, Table 1 note explicitly says "the two time-on-task rows are post-treatment". The main contrast results and adjusted means are in PDF p. 8, Section 3.4 and Figure 2; the additional duration-adjusted result is in PDF p. 9, Section 3.5. The measure rates breadth of perspectives within one essay, so its construct would be flexibility, not across-people diversity. No unadjusted arm means or eligible alternative contrast are printed.

not_extracted.what: Baseline writing-ability levels and randomization-balance tests
not_extracted.reason: The baseline essay was completed before randomized assignment and served as a covariate, so its stand-alone levels are not an outcome of assigned AI assistance. See PDF p. 4, Table 1; PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Section 2.6. Baseline-to-transfer change scores are retained separately; baseline SDs are not substituted for change-score SDs.

not_extracted.what: Self-report trait and process measures: autonomous cognitive offloading, reflective thinking, critical-thinking disposition, metacognitive monitoring, intrinsic motivation/interest, effort, AI-use frequency, and manipulation-check items
not_extracted.reason: These are questionnaire or self-report measures, not creativity or diversity scored on produced work. See PDF p. 6, Section 2.7; PDF p. 7, Sections 3.1–3.3; PDF p. 8, Table 3. Descriptive scale statistics and reliability estimates do not supply randomized output contrasts.

not_extracted.what: Workflow-fidelity and process outcomes: outline submission, unrevised AI-content adoption, AI-call counts, and time on task in either phase
not_extracted.reason: These measure compliance, tool use, or task duration rather than rated creativity or diversity across participants’ outputs. The adoption share compares a participant’s writing with offered model text, not different people’s outputs. See PDF p. 4, Table 1; PDF p. 5, Section 2.4; PDF p. 7, Sections 3.1–3.2; PDF p. 9, Section 3.5.

not_extracted.what: H3 trait-prediction models for reasoning quality, idea diversity, and originality, and trait-scale psychometric analyses
not_extracted.reason: The predictors are measured dispositions, not randomized AI assignments; the factor, reliability, validity, correlation, and incremental-prediction statistics are not treatment contrasts. The earlier scale-development samples are cited background, not additional experiments in this paper. See PDF p. 6, Section 2.7; PDF p. 8, Table 3; PDF pp. 9–10, Section 3.8.

not_extracted.what: Exploratory metacognitive-monitoring and intrinsic-motivation mediation analyses, including the mediator-adjusted direct effect on reasoning quality
not_extracted.reason: Mediation paths and direct effects conditioning on post-treatment mediators are explicitly outside extraction scope under Rule 5. See PDF pp. 10–11, Section 3.9.

not_extracted.what: Exploratory associations of AI-content adoption and prior outline submission with unaided reasoning
not_extracted.reason: These regressions use post-assignment behaviors as predictors, not the full-sample randomized-arm contrasts. The paper explicitly describes the process indices as consequences of the assigned workflow and the analyses as convergent description. See PDF p. 11, Section 3.10.

not_extracted.what: Comparisons of excluded versus retained participants and of AI-screen-flagged versus other No-AI responses
not_extracted.reason: These are selection or screening subgroups rather than randomized-arm contrasts; the within-No-AI reasoning means must not be treated as an AI-treatment comparison. See PDF p. 3, Section 2.2, and PDF p. 6, Section 2.6.

open_items: The paper prints no unadjusted arm means or baseline-only-adjusted treatment contrasts for originality or within-essay flexibility. All main ANCOVAs condition on same-phase time on task, which is post-treatment. These missing eligible statistics cannot be replaced by the plotted adjusted means (PDF pp. 4, 6–8).

The baseline-to-transfer reasoning change paragraph supplies no change-score SDs/SEs, pairwise differences, pairwise uncertainty, or analysis-specific participant counts (PDF p. 12, Section 4.5). Its omnibus test cannot be assigned to individual pairs or used to infer counts.

Reasoning quality is retained as usefulness following S1-O1 of the reconciled screening form because the rubric judges the content of arguments. Its boundary with the Review 1 writing-proficiency exclusion should be checked at reconciliation; a decision that this reasoning-only rubric is writing proficiency would also exclude the change-score records.
Qwen3.5 is named, but the release year, exact pinned model identifier, and sampling-parameter values are not printed; no release year is inferred from the publication date (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5).

Participants are described as Chinese-speaking students and early-career workers recruited online, but residence country is not stated (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, Section 4.5). Rater professional credentials are not reported (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6).

The power paragraph gives an achieved-cell range of 209–225 (PDF pp. 6–7, Section 2.8), whereas the primary arm counts repeatedly printed in Section 2.2 and Table 2 are 222, 225, and 212. The explicit participant-flow counts are used for the study, without resolving the power-paragraph discrepancy.

No appendix or separate supplement is identified in the complete supplied document or on-file supplement manifest. Full instructions, model configuration, rubric, de-identified data, and analysis materials are offered on request, and were not available in the files used (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5; PDF p. 13, Data availability statement).
notes: The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through the references and final page. Tables and figures were checked against the PDF first; Tables 1–4 were inspected with pymupdf text/table extraction, and Figure 2 was also rendered in memory. No other file was created. Study eligibility and estimate eligibility differ here: randomized human assistance and output ratings qualify the study, while extraction-spec Rule 5 excludes every main ANCOVA because it includes same-phase time measured after assignment. This applies to Phase 2 as well as Phase 1. Only the printed baseline-to-transfer arm change means are retained, once for each arm pairing already present in the paper. No pairwise differences or totals are calculated. In PDF p. 12, Section 4.5, the accompanying statistic is "between-arm diﬀerence in change scores F(2, 656) = 15.66, p < 0.0001". This is an omnibus test, not any pairwise test; it is therefore not placed in estimates[*].stats.test or p_value. Reasoning-quality scope is made explicit for reconciliation. PDF p. 6, Section 2.6 defines it as: "Reasoning quality captured the clarity of the thesis, the relevance and suﬃciency of evidence, the coherence of the reasoning, and the handling of counterarguments;" The screening form classifies this output-quality rubric as usefulness; the extraction retains that classification rather than treating it as a language-proficiency composite. Idea diversity is within-essay flexibility, not diversity across people; no across_people outcome is reported. Figure 2 contains unlabeled adjusted arm means, SE bars and contrast intervals; no value is read from axes or estimated from the graphics. There are no printed Phase-1 AI-versus-No-AI outcome contrasts. The unaided task followed the assisted task by 15–20 minutes in the same session (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1), so timing is immediate and no delay in days is calculated. Topic counterbalancing does not randomize AI/no-AI phase order. The study was not formally preregistered; the internal plan named Dependent versus No-AI on Phase-2 reasoning as primary (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1.1), not the change-score presentation retained here. Primary analysis counts are modified intention-to-treat, not all randomized participants (PDF p. 7, Section 2.8). No shared sample is reported; the paper states that the present sample is independent of the earlier DACOS development samples (PDF p. 6, Section 2.7).
